text:
Now SQL: average number of bonds per iodine atom. Count bonds where atom1 or atom2 is an iodine atom, divided by number of iodine atoms.

Let me write:

WITH iod AS (SELECT atom_id FROM atom WHERE element='i'),
b AS (SELECT atom_id AS a FROM connected UNION ALL SELECT atom_id2 FROM connected)
SELECT CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM iod) FROM b JOIN iod ON b.a = iod.atom_id;

Simple and avoids correlated subquery.

input.sql: WITH iod AS (SELECT atom_id FROM atom WHERE element = 'i'), ends AS (SELECT atom_id AS a FROM connected UNION ALL SELECT atom_id2 AS a FROM connected) SELECT CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM iod) AS avg_bonds FROM ends JOIN iod ON ends.a = iod.atom_id;
